events.title: Atari ST released
events.summary: Atari began shipping the ST line in June 1985 — a Motorola 68000 computer with MIDI ports and GEM desktop environment.
events.about: The Atari ST became the platform of choice for MIDI musicians and European demo coders — built-in MIDI DIN ports connected synthesizers without extra hardware. Developers used 68000 assembly and C; games and music software pushed its custom chips. It competed with the Amiga for the 16-bit home creative market.

narrative.whyChosen: The Atari ST was the dominant home computer for MIDI music production in the 1980s.
narrative.whyImportant: It brought affordable 16-bit computing and built-in MIDI to musicians and hobbyist developers.
narrative.problemSolved: Musicians needed a computer with native MIDI I/O and decent graphics without workstation prices.
